feature.label: Ijams Park
feature.title: The final bow: Shakespeare's last four nights at Ijams Park
feature.deck: This time it's real — the 36th Knoxville Shakespeare festival ends Sunday. Henry V plays Thursday (pay-what-you-can) and Saturday; The Merry Wives of Windsor takes Friday and the festival's last night.

facts.label: Sun Aug 9
facts.value: Merry Wives — the festival's last bow

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: A chair or blanket · parking free 30 min before

body.text: Two weeks ago we called the wrong weekend Shakespeare's last and had to take it back. This time the calendar and the company agree: the 36th Knoxville Shakespeare festival plays its final four nights on the Ijams Park lawn this weekend, and when Falstaff takes his last bow Sunday evening, that's the season.

King Henry V opens the farewell Thursday — and Thursday is still pay-what-you-can, so the cheapest possible way into professional Shakespeare remains the week's opener. Merry Wives takes Friday. Saturday is your last chance at Henry V — Agincourt, the St. Crispin's Day speech, all of it — and Sunday night The Merry Wives of Windsor closes the whole festival. Doors at 7, curtain 7:30, every night.

Twenty dollars a ticket except Thursday; kids under fifteen free through Penny for the Arts; parking free starting thirty minutes before curtain; the lawn is the seating, so bring the chair or the blanket; and if it rains, the show moves indoors rather than away. After Sunday, the lawn goes back to the fireflies until next summer.

stories.title: Before the theater: Thursday is Election Day
stories.deck: State and federal primaries, polls open 8 AM to 8 PM. Vote first, then go watch Henry V rally the troops.

facts.label: Next Thu
facts.value: Kerbela apartments hearing · Aug 13 · agenda item 44

body.text: One piece of civic business before the weekend fun: Thursday, August 6 is Election Day — state and federal primaries, polls open 8 in the morning to 8 at night. Check your precinct with the Knox County Election Commission if you've moved. Conveniently, the polls close half an hour after curtain at Ijams Park, so the truly efficient can vote on the way to Agincourt.

The other civic date on the horizon: the roughly 220-unit apartment plan for the old Kerbela Shriners Temple site goes back before the Administrative Review Committee on August 13, agenda item 44, with staff recommendations due to post about a week out. We'll have the full picture in the next episode.

stories.label: Kern's
stories.title: The Ho'down takes root at Kern's — now every other Friday
stories.deck: Line dancing graduates from one-off to standing date, The Big Pink covers The Band, and the weekend closes on jazz and easy Sunday covers.

facts.label: Fri Aug 7
facts.value: The Big Pink (The Band covers) 5 PM · Ho'down Social 8–11 PM

body.text: The country dancing at Kern's is officially a habit now: the Ho'down Social returns Friday night, eight to eleven, this time with Cowtown Studios calling the two-steps and line dances — and it's the first date of a new every-other-Friday series that runs into December. No partner required, boots encouraged, beginners the whole point.

Friday's warm-up act is a treat for the classic-rock faithful: The Big Pink plays the music of The Band from five to eight, which means you can go from "The Weight" straight into a line dance. Saturday brings Milkshake Fatty's jazzy instrumental takes on pop songs, six to nine, and Sunday afternoon Chase Countiss plays covers and originals from one to four. Friday also keeps the standing half-price wine bottles at Eggspectation from three o'clock on — the quiet-table option while the boots stomp outside.

stories.title: Ijams Park beyond the stage: a sold-out river and the gentlest Sunday of the year
stories.deck: Friday's evening paddle sold out — register earlier next time — Saturday belongs to the storytellers, and Sunday stacks a sound bath, a stained-glass workshop, and yoga back to back.

facts.label: Aug 15
facts.value: Hummingbird Festival — live bird banding, 7 AM–1 PM

body.text: A note of neighborhood pride disguised as bad news: Friday's guided evening paddle on the river is sold out. The boats fill faster every week, which tells you something about this place — if a sunset kayak is on your list, grab the next date on the Ijams Park calendar the day it posts. Saturday is friendlier to procrastinators: free storytelling at the Nature Playscape from ten to noon, no registration, just kids and a good book under the trees.

Sunday might be the softest slate Ijams Park runs all year: a sound bath meditation at ten — bring a mat and get washed in singing bowls — a stained-glass workshop at eleven where you leave with a heart, black bear, or moth suncatcher of your own making (eighty dollars, materials included, ages fourteen up), and Self Care Sunday yoga in the trees at 11:30. Do all three and you'll float home.

And a look-ahead worth inking in: the Hummingbird Festival lands Saturday, August 15, with live bird-banding sessions from seven to one — the closest most of us will ever get to a bird that weighs less than a nickel. More on that in the next episode.

stories.label: Suttree Landing
stories.title: The specials board: the full margarita ladder, and dog bingo
stories.deck: Earl's runs a different deal every single day of the weekend, and Alliance Brewing closes it with bingo you play for the dogs.

facts.label: Sun
facts.value: Earl's — $7 mimosas & bloodys all day · Bow Wow Bingo at Alliance 2 PM

body.text: Earl's on the waterfront runs the full ladder this weekend, a different rung every day: ten-dollar Patrón mango margaritas Thursday and nine-dollar spicy pineapple ritas Friday, both four to six with a dollar off liquor, beer, and wine; then the weekend opens up — eight-dollar house margaritas all day Saturday, and seven-dollar mimosas and Bloody Marys all day Sunday. Plan the weekend by rung.

And over on Sevier Avenue, Alliance Brewing hosts Bow Wow Bingo Sunday at two — bingo with the proceeds going to the dogs, per Inside of Knoxville's planner, with an RSVP requested. A beer, a bingo card, and a good cause within walking distance of the river: that's a Sunday.
